rules.title: tuple_count_of::<T>() yields tuple arity
rules.statement: tuple_count_of::<T>() evaluates at compile time to an i64 literal equal to the number of element types of T when T is a tuple type, and to 0 for any non-tuple T.

rules.title: field_count_of::<T>() yields struct field count
rules.statement: field_count_of::<T>() evaluates at compile time to an i64 literal equal to the number of declared fields of T when T is a struct (or zoned struct) type; for any non-struct or unresolvable T it is 0. The struct template is matched by name, preferring a package-qualified match (T.pkg) and falling back to name-only.

rules.title: field_names_of::<T>() yields array of field-name strings
rules.statement: field_names_of::<T>() evaluates at compile time to an array [&str; N] whose elements are the declared field names of struct T in declaration order; for non-struct or unresolvable T it is the empty array. Struct lookup prefers a package-qualified match and falls back to name-only.

rules.title: type-reflection intrinsics produce [Type; N] descriptors
rules.statement: args_of::<T>(), type_refs_of, tuple_elems_of, typelist_tail, and field_types_of each evaluate at compile time to an array [Type; N] of struct literals. Each Type element has fields {kind: u32 = the type's kind tag, name: &str = the type's printed name, size: i64 = size_of, align: i64 = align_of, uid: u64 = a canonical 64-bit type hash}. N and the per-element source types are determined per-intrinsic (see related rules).

rules.title: args_of::<T>() yields T's generic type arguments
rules.statement: args_of::<T>() produces a [Type; N] descriptor array of the generic type-arguments of T (in order); for a non-generic T the array is empty.

rules.title: typelist_tail::<T>() drops the first type argument
rules.statement: typelist_tail::<T>() produces a [Type; N] descriptor array of T's generic type-arguments excluding the first (i.e. the tail beginning at index 1); empty when T has fewer than two type arguments.

rules.title: tuple_elems_of::<T>() yields tuple element types
rules.statement: tuple_elems_of::<T>() produces a [Type; N] descriptor array of the element types of T when T is a tuple; empty otherwise.

rules.title: field_types_of::<T>() yields substituted struct field types
rules.statement: field_types_of::<T>() produces a [Type; N] descriptor array of the field types of struct (or zoned struct) T in declaration order, with the struct template's type parameters substituted by T's actual type arguments (positional binding of template params to T.type_args); empty for non-struct or unresolvable T.

rules.title: Debug formatting of tuples is synthesized element-wise
rules.statement: Debug formatting of a tuple T=(t0,..,t_{n-1}) emits an open delimiter, then for each element the element's Debug rendering separated by separators, then a close delimiter (a distinct close form for n==1). Each non-tuple element is formatted by a recursive `fmt` method-call dispatched on the element's Debug impl; a nested tuple element recurses through the same builder. A &[u8] slice element is formatted as `str`.

rules.title: Type-pack expansion in call arguments
rules.statement: A pack-expansion call argument over a type-pack variable expands at monomorphization to one argument per bound pack element, each a per-element variable reference into the callee signature; when the callee is a generic template, the pack's element types are also appended to the call's type arguments.

rules.title: Const-pack expansion in call arguments
rules.statement: A pack-expansion call argument over a const-pack variable expands at monomorphization to one literal-int argument per bound element, each carrying the pack element's underlying numeric type.

rules.title: Generic trait-static dispatch rewrites the receiver-type prefix
rules.statement: A call whose mangled callee is `[pkg.]<DT>__<method...>` where DT is a generic type parameter bound by the substitution map is rewritten to dispatch on the concrete bound type: the `<DT>` prefix is replaced by the concrete receiver name and the substituted type's package (falling back to the original callee package). The concrete name is the concrete struct name for a struct, the mangled enum name `<base>__<arg>...` for an enum, `$ref_`/`$mut_ref_` prefixed for a `&T`/`&mut T` receiver, and the printed type name otherwise; a `&[u8]` receiver name is normalized to `str`.

rules.title: Inferring method type-args at trait-static dispatch
rules.statement: When a rewritten trait-static call carries no explicit type arguments but the target method has method-level type parameters, the call is re-formed into a template callee and supplied inferred type arguments so the correct specialization is instantiated; without this a `.collect::<C>()`-style call would lower to an un-parameterized callee that is never emitted.

rules.title: Associated-type projection disambiguates multi-impl trait-static dispatch
rules.statement: When trait-static dispatch on `Self::method` is ambiguous among multiple trait-qualified candidates `<Self>__<Trait>$G..__<m>` distinguished only by a trait type-argument that is not a method parameter but an associated type of an argument, the correct candidate is selected by associated-type projection: for each argument type, find non-blanket impls whose target unifies with it, substitute the impl's type-params, and mangle the impl's trait type-args; pick the unique candidate whose `$G..` token an argument carries. A re-instantiable template is preferred over an already-monomorphized spec sharing the same token.
rules.uncertainty: Selection mechanism inferred from candidate-gathering and token-matching logic; only the disambiguation start is within this unit (completion continues past L3172).
